definition: Universal Networking Language (UNL) is a declarative formal language specifically designed to represent semantic data extracted from natural language texts.
details: It can be used as a pivot language in interlingual machine translation systems or as a knowledge representation language in information retrieval applications.

explainer.lead: Universal Networking Language is a declarative formal language designed to represent semantic data extracted from natural language texts. It matters as a pivot for interlingual machine translation and as a knowledge representation language in information retrieval.

tiers.eli5: It's a neutral in-between language that text gets translated into, so it can then be turned into any other language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use UNL as an interlingua in machine translation or as a knowledge representation layer in retrieval applications, converting source text into its semantic representation first. A pitfall is the overhead of extracting and maintaining that semantic representation accurately.
tiers.paperLevel: A declarative formal language specifically designed to represent semantic data extracted from natural language texts; usable as a pivot language in interlingual machine translation or as a knowledge representation language in information retrieval.

explainer.example: A translation system converts a source sentence into UNL semantic data and then generates the target-language text from that representation.
